name: Xiamen Hithium Energy Storage Technology Co., Ltd. (厦门海辰储能科技股份有限公司)
employees: ~7,650 (FY2024, company ESG figure via aggregator); ~10,500 (Mar 2026, third-party workforce estimate)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Hithium has reached top-two global ESS cell scale as a stationary-only specialist riding a large-cell, LDES-native product ladder; we assess financing — after three failed listing attempts — is the primary vulnerability. BACKGROUND: Hithium is a pure-play stationary energy-storage battery manufacturer founded in December 2019 by former CATL engineer Wu Zuyu. It mass-produces prismatic LFP cells purpose-built for storage (280Ah, 314Ah, 587Ah, 1175Ah, and 1300Ah classes), sodium-ion cells, and integrated battery energy storage systems (∞Block and ∞Power DC blocks up to 6.9 MWh) for utility-scale, C&I, and residential applications, selling to grid operators, developers, and integrators in 20+ countries. The company remains private as of August 2026: an A-share attempt was withdrawn in 2023 and two Hong Kong Main Board applications (March 2025, October 2025) both lapsed, the second in April 2026. AIDC LENS (v5): Hithium entered the AI-data-center race with '∞Power Solutions for AI Data Center' — a four-SKU lithium-sodium 'full-duration' portfolio soft-launched for the US at RE+ 2025 (Sep 2025) and formally launched at its Third Eco-Day (Dec 12, 2025) — positioned as a full-duration energy backbone (millisecond sodium buffering, 2h/4h diesel-replacement backup, 8h renewable pairing) rather than a compliance-grade UPS: no NOGRR 282/LVRT claims, no use of the word UPS, and, eight months on, zero named AIDC customers, pilots, or UPS-integrator partnerships anywhere. The US socket it targets is being defined by ON.energy's FEOC-clean medium-voltage AI UPS (5 GW Crusoe deployment) while the FEOC/tariff stack fences Hithium out of ITC-driven and hyperscale-visible procurement — leaving safe-harbored, merchant, and non-US channels as the line's realistic landing zones.
ecosystemRole: One of the world's largest ESS cell suppliers — No. 5 globally in 2023 (>15 GWh, InfoLink), No. 3 in 2024 (35.1 GWh, ~11% share, behind CATL and EVE), and Top 2 in both total and utility-scale ESS battery shipments for 2025 (InfoLink/SMM/ICC); cumulative shipments passed 100 GWh in August 2025. Manufacturing: Xiamen HQ, Chongqing (world's first WEF 'Lighthouse Factory' in energy-storage batteries, Jan 2026), Shandong, a 10 GWh/yr module + system plant in Mesquite, Texas (first shipments Aug 2025), and a committed €400M cell + BESS gigafactory in Navarre, Spain (target 2027). In the US AIDC web (see the relationship-web deliverable), Hithium's access runs through battery-buying owners — the anchor is Jupiter Power (3 GWh supply + the 2.8 GWh Trimount design win, EFSB-approved Feb 2026), with Microgrid Networks NYC (55 MW/290 MWh) the second-largest named US relationship — while EPCs install owner-furnished systems and utility self-build remains effectively closed to Chinese cells.

productsAndServices.name: Utility-scale LFP storage cells (∞Cell line)
productsAndServices.description: Prismatic LFP cells purpose-built for stationary storage — the core product and the company's founding premise (storage-optimized cells, not repurposed EV cells). Current catalog: ESS Cell 280Ah (≥7,000 cycles, ≥159.2 Wh/kg), ESS Cell 314Ah (≥13,000 cycles, ≥173.2 Wh/kg — the volume workhorse in ∞Block systems), ∞Cell 587Ah (≥11,000 cycles, ≈185 Wh/kg / ≈413 Wh/L; mass production and first deliveries from Xiamen since 2025), ∞Cell 1175Ah (world's first mass-produced kAh-class cell — Chongqing, from June 2025; ≥11,000 cycles, ≥180 Wh/kg / ≥400 Wh/L), ∞Cell 1300Ah for 8-hour LDES (≥10,000 cycles, ≥190 Wh/kg / ≥406 Wh/L; mass delivery targeted Q4 2026), and the ∞Cell 650Ah debuted at SNEC 2026 (deliveries expected 2027; detailed specs not yet published). The 587Ah is derived from the 1175Ah platform; Hithium's stated technical differentiator is ultra-thick electrode technology.
highlights: Cells supplied to integrators including NHOA, Risen Energy, and (formerly) Powin alongside Hithium's own systems
∞Cell 1175Ah earned UL 1973 and UL 9540A certification at SNEC 2025
Both 587Ah and 1175Ah already used in GWh-scale BESS installations (Energy-Storage.News large-cell comparison, 2026)
Intertek CEA (Jul 2026) projects 587Ah-class cells driving BESS cost declines through 2027 — module/rack-level energy density gains of 60–80% from the new cell architecture
productsAndServices.positioning: One of only two suppliers (with CATL) shipping 500Ah+ class cells at GWh scale as of early 2026, and the only one in mass production above 1,000Ah. Vs named competitors in the large-format race: CATL's 587Ah (≥12,000 cycles, 430–434 Wh/L, 96.5% RTE) leads on volumetric density and efficiency; EVE's 628Ah 'Mr. Big' (386 Wh/L, 193.3 Wh/kg) on gravimetric density; Hithium competes on cycle life, the ultra-thick-electrode 1175Ah/1300Ah kAh-class tier no rival mass-produces, and purpose-built LDES design. As a stationary-only specialist it avoids EV-cell allocation conflicts that diversified rivals (CATL, BYD, EVE) manage.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct cell supply to system integrators and OEMs (NHOA, Risen, formerly Powin), alongside captive consumption in Hithium's own ∞Block/∞Power DC blocks — a dual model: merchant cell vendor and vertically integrated system supplier. A technology-licensing channel was explored (Reliance Industries, India) but collapsed in January 2026 under Chinese export-control tightening on battery technology transfer.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utility-scale storage developers and integrators globally; long-duration (4–8h) procurement programs; grid operators in China, the Middle East, Europe, Australia, Southeast Asia, and the Americas
productsAndServices.roadmap: ∞Cell 1300Ah mass delivery Q4 2026 (8-hour LDES); ∞Cell 650Ah deliveries expected 2027; continued kAh-class scaling per the SNEC 2026 large-capacity portfolio strategy

productsAndServices.name: Containerized utility-scale systems (∞Block / ∞Power)
productsAndServices.description: Factory-integrated DC blocks sold as the building block of utility projects: ∞Block 4.180 MWh and 5.016 MWh (314Ah cells, 20-ft container), ∞Power 6.25 MWh 2h/4h variants in a standard 20-ft container (2h: 587Ah cells, 8×1P416S; 4h: 1175Ah cells, 4×1P416S), the ∞Power 6.9 MWh 8-hour-native LDES system (1300Ah cell, 4×1P416S, 55.2 MWh per 8-unit block; mass delivery Q4 2026), the transport-optimized 10-ft modular ∞Power Flexsso (3.125/6.25 MWh 4h configurations, <26 t per unit, ~423 kWh/m², ≥95% DC round-trip efficiency; first deliveries Q2 2026), an ∞Power 10+ MWh solution unveiled at SNEC 2026, and a hardened 'Desert Eagle' variant rated -30°C to 60°C with multi-layer insulation and sandstorm sealing.
highlights: 4 GWh Saudi Electricity Company LDES projects (Tabuk and Hail, with Alfanar; reported RMB 2.6B supply deal; ∞Cell 1175Ah in 6.25 MWh containers; commissioning targeted 2026)
2 GWh to Ukraine via KNESS Group from Q1 2026; 2 GWh Eastern Europe framework with Bulgaria's Solarpro (587Ah/1175Ah systems)
3 GWh LDES framework with Brawn Capital for Asia-Pacific by 2030 (Mar 2026, incl. Flexsso units; first 300 MWh in 2027)

366 MWh with Turbo Energy for 15 European industrial sites (EES Europe, Jun 2026; 21× 6.25 MWh containers delivered); Statkraft's Montes de Cierzo wind-farm BESS in Navarre, Spain — 6× ∞Block 5.016 MWh, 30.1 MWh (Jul 2026)
Prospectus customers include Jupiter Power, Lightsource bp, Samsung C&T, Datang Group, and Longyuan Power
productsAndServices.positioning: Competes in the 6+ MWh 20-ft DC-block class against CATL (EnerX/TENER), BYD (MC Cube), EVE, Sungrow and Tesla-class integrated offerings; differentiates on cell-to-system vertical integration around its own large-format cells (fewer cells per container — the 1022 kWh C&I cabinet claims a 70% cell-count reduction from 1175Ah cells), 8-hour-native LDES design rather than stretched 2–4h products, and harsh-environment engineering (Desert Eagle; -30°C to 60°C). Australia positioning explicitly targets jurisdictions mandating 8-hour duration (NSW: 28 GWh by 2033).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: DC blocks direct to developers, EPCs, and IPPs (Alfanar, KNESS, Solarpro, Statkraft, Turbo Energy, Brawn Capital), typically with the buyer or a partner supplying PCS/EMS integration; long-term O&M attached on flagship projects (Saudi SEC); US deliveries assembled at Mesquite, Texas
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utility-scale developers and grid operators (Middle East, Europe incl. Ukraine reconstruction, Australia, Southeast Asia, North America); markets with LDES mandates or duration-linked tenders; transport-constrained sites (Flexsso)
productsAndServices.roadmap: ∞Power 6.9 MWh 8h mass delivery Q4 2026; ∞Power 10+ MWh class productization (SNEC 2026 debut, deliveries expected with the 650Ah cell from 2027); Flexsso rollout across APAC (Brawn) and Europe from Q2 2026

productsAndServices.name: ∞Power Solutions for AI Data Center (the AIDC line)
productsAndServices.description: Four-SKU lithium-sodium portfolio formally launched at the Third Eco-Day, Xiamen (Dec 12, 2025) as the 'world's first lithium-sodium full-duration AIDC energy storage solution', after a US soft-launch at RE+ 2025 (Sep 10, 2025): ∞Power N2.28MWh 1h sodium-ion (the 'first line of defense' — millisecond-scale smoothing of GPU load swings claimed at up to 70% within tens of milliseconds, sub-10ms PCS response, >25-year service life), ∞Power 6.25MWh 2h and 4h lithium units (silent zero-carbon diesel-genset replacement, claimed >20% lower lifecycle cost for backup up to 4 hours), and the ∞Power 6.9MWh 8h unit (generation-side renewable pairing targeting 80%+ renewable penetration; claimed to compress data-center power buildout 'from five-to-ten years to one-to-two'). Trade press adds 240V/400V compatibility today with 800V HVDC anticipated. The 8h SKU migrated from the 6.25 MWh design (Sep 2025) to the 1300Ah-based 6.9 MWh container (Dec 2025).
productsAndServices.positioning: A full-duration energy backbone, deliberately NOT a compliance-grade UPS: Hithium makes no ERCOT NOGRR 282/LVRT ride-through claims and avoids the word UPS — the substantive contrast with ON.energy's AI UPS (medium-voltage, ride-through-certified, 5 GW Crusoe anchor, FEOC-clean stack), the category benchmark. Against Chinese peers: CATL's TENER Stack 9 MWh is 'engineered for AI-driven data centres' and TENER Sodium delivers from Sep 2026; EVE goes deeper into the rack (BBU/UPS cells); Sungrow fields the most architecturally complete grid-to-chip offer (PCS + storage + SST); Tesla's Megapack 3/Megablock carries the US-made advantage; Vertiv's EnergyCore Grid validates BESS-UPS convergence from the incumbent side. Hithium's unique angle is the lithium+sodium 1h-8h breadth under one brand and 8h-native duration; its gap is zero anchor customers and the NDAA/FEOC fence on US campuses.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct and via developers/integrators; no AIDC-specific channel, UPS-maker partnership, or named customer disclosed as of Aug 2026
productsAndServices.targetSegments: AI data centers and campuses — grid-side buffering, backup replacement, and renewable-paired generation-side storage; realistically non-US and merchant/safe-harbored US buyers under the current policy stack
productsAndServices.roadmap: ∞Power8 (6.9 MW/55.2 MWh block) mass delivery Q4 2026; scale volumes from 2027 (Chongqing + Heze, 70+ GWh planned); sodium N162Ah 'GWh mass production' was planned for Q4 2025 but remains unconfirmed — the sodium SKU's commercial availability is unproven

productsAndServices.name: Sodium-ion products (∞Cell N162Ah / ∞Power N)
productsAndServices.description: The ∞Cell N162Ah (launched December 2024) is billed as the first sodium-ion battery specialized for utility-scale storage — sodium iron pyrophosphate (NFPP) cathode with hard-carbon anode, 2.82 V nominal, ≥95.2 Wh/kg / ≥173 Wh/L, ~94.2% retention after 4,000 cycles, ≥20,000-cycle life, 94% energy efficiency, and a -40°C to 60°C operating window; paired with the ∞Power N 2.28 MWh (1h) containerized system. Passed a Chinese national-level product assessment in 2025 per the company.
highlights: GWh-scale mass production planned from Q4 2025
Showcased at SNEC 2026 alongside the LFP line — positioned for high-cycling short-duration and extreme-cold applications
productsAndServices.positioning: Against sodium-ion rivals (CATL Naxtra, BYD, HiNA, Envision), Hithium's angle is the same as its LFP story: the only sodium cell purpose-designed for stationary storage rather than adapted from EV formats, with cycle life (≥20,000) and cold-weather range (-40°C) as the lead specs. Sodium remains a hedge/complement while LFP dominates volume — lower energy density (~95 Wh/kg vs 173+ for its own 314Ah LFP) keeps it niche until lithium prices or cold-climate demand shift the calculus.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Same channels as the LFP line — cells to integrators and complete ∞Power N systems direct
productsAndServices.targetSegments: High-cycle grid applications (frequency regulation), extreme-cold climates, and customers hedging lithium supply risk; company materials also point sodium LDES concepts at AI data-center storage
productsAndServices.roadmap: Volume ramp from the Q4 2025 mass-production start; no public capacity or next-generation cell disclosure as of Aug 2026

productsAndServices.name: C&I storage
productsAndServices.description: Cabinet-class liquid-cooled DC blocks for commercial & industrial sites: ∞Block 261 kWh (1P52S, 314Ah cells, 1350×1000×2350 mm), ∞Block 418 kWh (1P416S, 314Ah cells, 1350×1300×2350 mm), and the ∞Power 1022 kWh cabinet (1P34S on 1175Ah cells, 1000 V DC, 3.4 m² footprint — the large-cell architecture pushed down to C&I, cutting cell count ~70%).
highlights: 1 GWh three-year cooperation with DSS Solar (signed at SNEC 2026) targeting Vietnam's residential and C&I markets
productsAndServices.positioning: Competes with Sungrow PowerStack, CATL EnerOne-class cabinets, Sigenergy and a crowded Chinese C&I field; differentiation is cell heritage (utility-grade 314Ah/1175Ah cells with 10,000+ cycle life in C&I form factors) rather than software/VPP features, where dedicated C&I players lead.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Distributors, solar/storage installers, and regional partners (e.g. DSS Solar in Vietnam); also direct to industrial energy users via EPCs
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Factories, commercial buildings, and behind-the-meter peak-shaving/demand-charge customers in China, Southeast Asia, and Europe
productsAndServices.roadmap: 1175Ah-based C&I cabinets (∞Power 1022 kWh) scaling in 2026; Vietnam channel build-out via the DSS Solar agreement through 2029

productsAndServices.name: Residential & portable power (HeroEE / ARKVOLT lines)
productsAndServices.description: Consumer-grade LFP products: portable all-in-one power stations HeroEE 1 (1 kWh, 200 W), HeroEE LIGHT 1 (1 kWh, 500 W, integrated inverter + MPPT) and HeroEE 2 (2 kWh, 1,000 W, 11,000-cycle rating); the HeroEE MaxPower 8 AIO home unit (debuted SNEC 2026); and residential battery systems HeroEE 16 (16 kWh, expandable to 256 kWh) plus ARKVOLT L16 / L16S wall units (16.07 kWh, 51.2 V / 314Ah, 200 A).
highlights: 11,000-cycle claims across the HeroEE line — utility cell longevity marketed into consumer products
productsAndServices.positioning: A small adjacency, not a core business — competes against EcoFlow/Bluetti-class portables and Tesla Powerwall/BYD/Sungrow-class home batteries on cycle life and cell pedigree rather than brand or ecosystem software. Public disclosure of revenue contribution is minimal; the line chiefly demonstrates cell versatility and fills retail channels.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Retail/online channels and regional distribution partners (DSS Solar covers residential in Vietnam)
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Homeowners with rooftop solar, backup-power buyers, and off-grid/outdoor users
productsAndServices.roadmap: HeroEE MaxPower 8 AIO commercialization following its SNEC 2026 debut; no further public roadmap disclosed

productsAndServices.name: Localized manufacturing & delivery
productsAndServices.description: US module and full-BESS assembly in Mesquite, Texas (~484,000 sq ft, ~$200M, 10 GWh/yr, first shipments August 2025) serving North America as Chinese-import tariffs on battery products rise (7% → 26% in 2026); committed European cell + BESS production in Navarre, Spain (€400M JV with Sodena, ~700 jobs, €81M Spanish government grant, target 2027); Chongqing plant recognized as the WEF's first energy-storage-battery 'Lighthouse Factory' (Jan 2026); long-term O&M included in the Saudi SEC projects.
highlights: Texas plant positions Hithium among the first Chinese ESS makers with US BESS assembly (alongside LG ES's US push), partially insulating US sales from tariff escalation

A cell-technology licensing deal with India's Reliance Industries collapsed in Jan 2026 after Beijing tightened export controls on battery technology transfer; Hithium remains a Reliance BESS component partner per media reports
productsAndServices.positioning: Localization is the sales argument in tariff- and content-rule-constrained markets: US assembly for domestic-content procurement, planned Spanish cells for EU battery-regulation alignment (Flexsso is marketed as 'fully aligned with EU Battery Regulation').
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Localized assembly feeds the same direct developer/EPC channels; licensing as a channel is currently blocked by Chinese export controls
productsAndServices.targetSegments: US utility/IPP buyers needing domestic assembly; EU buyers under the EU Battery Regulation; Middle East projects with O&M attachments
productsAndServices.roadmap: Navarre, Spain cell + BESS plant targeted 2027; Texas capacity ramp toward the 10 GWh/yr nameplate

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Hithium has secured top-tier scale as a stationary-only specialist — Top 2 in 2025 ESS cell shipments behind CATL per InfoLink/SMM/ICC, with cumulative shipments past 100 GWh in August 2025.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the large-cell ladder (587→650→1175→1300Ah) feeding 6+ MWh blocks, with 8-hour-native LDES as the differentiated tier, is a deliberate policy fit — duration-mandating markets (NSW: 28 GWh by 2033) are the target.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the US (Mesquite, Texas) and EU (Navarre, Spain) plants insulate the order book against tariff and content rules; the €400M Spain commitment with a 2027 target is the pacing item.

(Moderate confidence) We assess financing capacity, not demand, is the constraint: three failed listing attempts (A-share 2023; two lapsed HKEX applications) against a capex-heavy expansion. Basis: prospectus filings and financial-media reporting.

(High confidence) We assess the AIDC line as a product-marketing position rather than a business as of Aug 2026: two launches, four SKUs, and specific engineering claims — but zero named customers, pilots, or UPS-integrator partnerships in any geography eight months after launch, a sodium SKU whose mass production remains unconfirmed, and a flagship 8h block whose deliveries begin only in Q4 2026. Its US path is additionally fenced by the policy stack; its realistic near-term landing zones are non-US campuses and merchant/tax-indifferent US buyers.

(High confidence) We assess the AIDC category's US terms are being set by ON.energy, not Hithium: the AI UPS is medium-voltage, ride-through-certified (NOGRR 282/LVRT), FEOC-clean by design, and anchored by a 5 GW Crusoe deployment — every attribute the ∞Power AIDC line lacks for US hyperscale buyers. Hithium's differentiators (lithium+sodium breadth, 8h-native duration, cost) matter most where the policy fence does not apply.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the Jupiter relationship — the US anchor — as strong but no longer exclusive-trending: the 3 GWh deal's completion is unconfirmed publicly, Trimount revenue sits years out behind remediation, and Jupiter's Nov 2025 Peak Energy sodium deal (720 MWh + up to 4 GWh reserved) plants a domestic supplier inside the account precisely on the chemistry Hithium markets as its next act. Defending the account on economics, delivery record, and augmentation terms is the highest-leverage US sales action available.

relationships.note: Founded by an ex-CATL engineer; #2 behind CATL in 2025 ESS shipments; ~10 pending lawsuits >RMB 240M.
relationships.context:
Hithium was founded in December 2019 by former CATL engineer Wu Zuyu (three of four executive directors are ex-CATL), and the rivalry is now litigated: roughly ten pending CATL-Hithium suits exceeding RMB 240M, flagged in Hithium's lapsed HKEX filings.

Commercially they bracket the market: InfoLink's FY2025 ranking puts Hithium Top 2 in both total and utility-scale ESS cell shipments behind CATL, and the product lines collide across large-format LFP (587Ah vs 1175Ah/1300Ah), sodium-ion (Naxtra/TENER Sodium vs ∞Cell N), and AIDC systems (TENER Stack 9 MWh vs ∞Power).

relationships.note: Anchor US account: 3 GWh supply plus the 2.8 GWh Trimount design win (EFSB-approved Feb 2026).
relationships.context:
Jupiter Power is the largest named US relationship in Hithium's book — a 3 GWh supply agreement plus the 2.8 GWh Trimount, Massachusetts design win that cleared the state EFSB in February 2026. Access runs through battery-buying owners like Jupiter while utility self-build stays effectively closed to Chinese cells.

The warning light: in November 2025 Jupiter signed a sodium-ion supply deal with US maker Peak Energy (720 MWh for 2027, up to 4 GWh reserved 2028-30) — supply-chain diversification that plants a domestic competing supplier inside the anchor account.
relationships.scale: 3 GWh supply + 2.8 GWh Trimount design win

Hithium's line is deliberately positioned as a full-duration energy backbone, not a compliance-grade UPS, leaving safe-harbored, merchant and non-US channels as its realistic landing zones.

relationships.context: EVE mass-produced the 628Ah class first, but Hithium is the only maker in mass production above 1,000Ah (∞Cell 1175Ah, 1300Ah announced) — one of only two suppliers (with CATL) shipping 500Ah+ cells at GWh scale by early 2026. InfoLink's FY2025 ranking put Hithium #2 and EVE #3 as the market doubled to 612 GWh. As diversified rivals (CATL, BYD, EVE) manage EV-cell allocation conflicts, Hithium's stationary-only focus is the differentiation.

Hithium's counter-positioning: purpose-designed stationary cells (8-hour-native LDES, harsh-environment engineering) versus formats adapted from EV lines.

The two also meet in the 6+ MWh DC-block class and home storage.

Tesla Powerwall also bounds the residential adjacency (HeroEE/ARKVOLT). The structural competitor for exactly the US demand Hithium's Texas assembly plant was built to chase.

relationships.context: ESS News paired the two in June 2025: Hithium and LG Energy Solution both began US battery manufacture into a tough American market — Hithium's Texas BESS assembly plant shipping first units while tariffs and FEOC rules mounted, LGES scaling domestic cells that qualify for ITC bonuses Hithium's content cannot. The comparison frames Hithium's whole US predicament.

financials.commentary: Private company — figures from HKEX prospectus filings and media summaries; no analyst consensus exists. Funding: Series B ~RMB 2.0B+ (Oct 2022), Series C >RMB 4.5B (~US$622M, Jul 2023); media valuation estimates RMB 25–30B (2025). Risk context flagged by financial media: three failed listing attempts (A-share withdrawn 2023; HKEX applications lapsed Sep 2025 and Apr 2026), 10+ CATL lawsuits claiming >RMB 240M, a partial equity freeze on the controlling shareholder's vehicle (Feb 2026, until Feb 2029), and FY2024 profitability's dependence on subsidies.
